body: It seems like this PR is generating a seek table just before playback. Does that mean it has to process the entire file before it can play it? Is there an extra start time overhead? Would it be possible to generate the seek table during importing instead?

> It seems like this PR is generating a seek table just before playback. Does that mean it has to process the entire file before it can play it? Is there an extra start time overhead?

It should be pretty much the same `minimp3_ex` did. Maybe slightly faster if you are loading then immediately playing, since generating a table only happens when instantiating a playback and not also when setting the data (thanks to `minimp3_ex` doing that in the validation phase too). And at least with the MRP audio, I noticed no overhead.

> Would it be possible to generate the seek table during importing instead?

Very likely, but that would be a different feature. For now I'd prefer solving the regression.

Just for fun, I have some more results, but with FPS unlocked: ### Godot 4.5.1: ### PR (seek table generation on playback instantiation): ### PR (seek table generation on setting data): ## Edit: this test was done in a hurry and might have inconsistent results. ## Edit 2: When I was testing this PR, having a gigantic frame rate was the result of forgetting to reimport. I forgot to re-import before testing. Nonetheless, the **result was the same after re-testing**. I was afraid that importing would have saved the seek table within the file, but that was not the case.
One last force push to keep up to date. It should be good to go.
